rows.axis: Continuous / in-flight (iteration-level) batching: max aggregate token throughput at high concurrency
rows.competitor: vLLM (PagedAttention + continuous batching); Orca (iteration-level scheduling, originator); TensorRT-LLM (in-flight batching)
rows.fak_doc: internal/modelengine/nativesched.go (NativeScheduler continuous batching); docs/benchmarks/published/HEADLINES.json (507693d73b C16 cohort 372.076 agg tok/s; 2e7682ba2a C24 783.7 tok/s); docs/benchmarks/published/rtx5080-inkling2-v060/perf-receipt-v2.json (C4_p2048 130.44 agg E2E)
rows.comparison_note: LIVE BATCHING SHIPPED ON CONVERGED MAIN, NO H100 vLLM/SGLANG HEAD-TO-HEAD YET: NativeScheduler (internal/modelengine) and CUDA cohorts ship live concurrent batching — RTX 5080 C16 ragged cohort prefill reaches 372.076 agg E2E tok/s (2.70x vs lockstep 137.702, commit 507693d73b), lockstep C24 f16 KV hits 783.7 agg decode tok/s (2e7682ba2a), and Wave-2 C4_p2048 HTTP reaches 130.44 agg E2E tok/s vs realugbun/llama.cpp 122.47 (C2_p512 still trails 121.16 vs 139.58). Because no comparable req/s or tok/s run exists against H100 SGLang/vLLM, verdict stays no-claim.

rows.fak_doc: internal/ggufload/inkling2loop_prefill.go (512-token chunked prefill) & internal/modelengine/nativesched.go; no TBT-SLO interference benchmark vs Nexus/Sarathi-Serve

rows.axis: Request scheduling and cache-aware routing (FCFS vs priority vs prefix/KV-cache-aware)
rows.competitor_source: SGLang: Zheng et al., 'Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs', arXiv:2312.07104, NeurIPS 2024 — published 50–99% hit-rate band.
rows.fak_doc: data.json row 'kv-hit-rate'; BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md L23 + 'RadixAttention Model Ladder' (FCFS 62.1% -> cache-aware 86.7% = 100% of optimal); artifact radixbench-qwen2.5-1.5b-q8-agents-fresh-20260619.json (verify workloads[0].cache_hit_rate=0.8666666666666667). Commit 92896a4.
rows.comparison_note: fak measured on-box: cache-aware (≡ DFS) scheduling recovers FCFS 62.1% → 86.7% = 100% of optimal, inside SGLang's published band. Split-reuse proven bit-identical to recompute (max|Δ|=0), so the hit is a real reuse, not a numerics shortcut. FENCE: 86.7% is on radixbench's synthetic 'agents' workload (deliberately cache-favorable); on a REAL tau2-airline trace fak's measured addressable purity is ~0.7% (CLAIMS vDSO unit 33/83) — so this is a same-workload-as-SGLang reuse-mechanism parity, not a promise of 86.7% on every production corpus.

rows.axis: Absolute aggregate tokens/s at scale on standardized hardware (MLPerf Inference)
rows.competitor: NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 x4 (288 Blackwell Ultra GPUs, TensorRT-LLM/Dynamo); MLPerf Inference v6.0 submitters (DeepSeek-R1 671B MoE, offline)
rows.fak_doc: No MLPerf submission or standardized-hardware aggregate tok/s in BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md. The only concurrent server number is the GPU server run (data.json 'served-throughput-vs-sglang', 1085.6 tok/s @ conc 64) which is fak-gateway-fronting-SGLang on non-MLPerf hardware/harness, not a standardized MLPerf result.
rows.comparison_note: EXCLUDE / out-of-scope for fak-native's mid-market 1-8 GPU target. MLPerf Inference v6.0 (2026-03-30) ranks aggregate tok/s on 288-GPU (4x GB300 NVL72) DeepSeek-R1 671B submissions (~2.494M tok/s). fak targets 1-8 GPU mid-market (26B-27B native on consumer/datacenter GPUs, plus GLM-5.2 MoE on 1 datacenter GPU) and has no MLPerf submission.

rows.competitor: Raw SGLang 0.5.10 (TP=8, no fak proxy), Qwen3.6-27B on an 8-GPU datacenter server — SAME load harness as fak-gateway (the gateway is the only delta); the absolute-latency SOTA bar is NVIDIA GenAI-Perf / vLLM benchmark_serving e2el percentile.
rows.competitor_source: experiments/qwen36/gpu-server-r4-20260622/compare.json (raw-SGLang vs fak-gateway, conc 1->128, P50 request latency @ conc 64); QWEN36-27B-GPU-SERVER-RESULTS.md s2
rows.comparison_note: WITNESSED gateway tax, the honest framing. Same 8-GPU datacenter server / Qwen3.6-27B / load harness, fak-gateway-in-front vs raw SGLang (the gateway is the only delta). At peak conc 64 fak's E2EL P50 is 9026.9 ms vs raw 7222.0 ms -> a +1804.9 ms (0.80x) end-to-end gateway tax. This is the FULL fak-in-front delta (proxy relay overhead PLUS the queueing induced by fak's lower peak throughput, 0.75x; see peak-serving-throughput-per-gpu), NOT just the in-process adjudication primitive (Decide 362 ns / AdmitChain <=87 us idle-box) which is only the small floor under it. fak fronts the backend and does NOT claim to win the raw-latency race; its value is the adjudication/coherence/measurement plane.

rows.competitor: Raw SGLang 0.5.10 (TP=8, no fak proxy), Qwen3.6-27B on an 8-GPU datacenter server — SAME load harness as fak-gateway (the gateway is the only delta); MLPerf Inference encodes its SLOs at P99 and production practice flags P99>>P50 as a saturation red flag.
rows.competitor_source: experiments/qwen36/gpu-server-r4-20260622/compare.json (raw-SGLang vs fak-gateway, conc 1->128, P99 request latency @ conc 64); QWEN36-27B-GPU-SERVER-RESULTS.md s2
rows.comparison_note: WITNESSED full request-latency tail on the same harness, fak-gateway-in-front vs raw SGLang. At peak conc 64 the committed distribution is fak P50/P95/P99 = 9026.9 / 9979.9 / 9997.6 ms vs raw 7222.0 / 8134.7 / 8157.9 ms; the P99 gateway tax is +1839.7 ms (0.82x). The tail is NOT widened by the gateway: fak's P99/P50 spread is 1.11x vs raw 1.13x, so fak shifts the WHOLE distribution by the ~+1.8 s tax rather than fattening the tail. Honest framing: fak fronts the backend and adds a measured tax, it does not claim to win the raw-latency race. (Sub-ms in-process primitive percentiles -- Decide 362 ns / AdmitChain <=87 us idle-box, BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md mac-m3pro-kernel-20260620 -- are the floor, not this under-load serving distribution.)

rows.axis: Peak served throughput per accelerator (model-served-by-engine, MLPerf-grounded)
rows.competitor: Raw SGLang 0.5.10 (TP=8, no fak proxy), Qwen3.6-27B on an 8-GPU datacenter server
rows.comparison_note: THE honest counter to the fleet 'lead' rows: this is the ONLY real concurrent-serving head-to-head against a LIVE SGLang process (same 8-GPU datacenter server / 27B / load harness, fak-in-front vs raw). fak TRAILS — it is the gateway/adjudication TAX: 0.60× worst (conc 8) → 0.75× at peak (conc 64) → ~0.97× converged at saturation (conc 128). fak's value here is the adjudication/coherence/measurement plane, NOT raw tok/s; the 4.1× fleet 'lead' is reuse-WORK eliminated on fak's own kernel held constant, a different axis from a throughput race against a tuned engine.

rows.axis: Single-stream (one chat) decode throughput on CPU
rows.competitor_source: llama.cpp llama-bench Metal, same M3 Pro box (build b9707); fak QWEN25-7B-RESULTS.md.
rows.comparison_note: fak explicitly does NOT target single-stream raw throughput — one chat → use llama.cpp. The gap narrows with model size (0.39× → 0.53×, 1.5B → 7B) toward the shared ~150 GB/s unified-memory bandwidth floor; arm64 still lacks the register-blocked int8 GEMM tile that already exists on x86.

rows.axis: Single-stream decode throughput on a consumer GPU
rows.competitor: realugbun/llama.cpp fork (2eb2530e) and upstream llama.cpp (ad50351f5) on RTX 5080 (-ngl 99)
rows.competitor_source: docs/benchmarks/published/aegis-inkling2-fork-parity/RESULTS.md (realugbun 119.47 tok/s, upstream llama.cpp 80.99 tok/s on same RTX 5080, 2026-11-24).
rows.comparison_note: HW-WITNESSED on RTX 5080 16 GB (sm_120f, Inkling-2-Mini-UD-Q3_K_XL): v0.60.0 in-process decode reaches 122.34 tok/s (TestInkling2CUDADecodeBench, kv=f16), and interleaved ABBA fork parity reaches 119.89 vs realugbun/llama.cpp 119.47 tok/s (1.51x upstream llama.cpp 80.99). Different harnesses (Go bench vs llama-bench), so read as parity, not a lead; at depth 1946 plain decode still trails the fork (88.97 vs 113.81 tok/s).

rows.comparison_note: HW-WITNESSED on RTX 5080 16 GB (sm_120f, Inkling-2-Mini-UD-Q3_K_XL): fak executes the checkpoint's NVFP4-quantized experts via native SM120 NVFP4 W4A4 grouped prefill (default at 27355b23dd), reaching 5861.0 tok/s HTTP pp512 server prompt rate (1.95x realugbun/llama.cpp fork 3012.4 tok/s, 2.73x upstream llama.cpp 2144.6 tok/s on the exact same UD-Q3_K_XL GGUF — llama.cpp runs its standard CUDA UD-Q3_K_XL kernels, NOT NVFP4 W4A4 activations), and 6037.6/6038.2/6033.9 vs 3337.4/3537.8/3648.6 tok/s at C2/C4/C8 pooled median (rev e7ad0c8dee5, 1 output token). HONEST FENCES: (1) server prompt rate only — on that C1 pp512 run median first visible token still trailed (1165.6 vs 195.5 ms), though Wave-2 C4_p2048 HTTP TTFT leads at 2017.61 vs 3718.34 ms (rtx5080-inkling2-v060); (2) on dense Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M (RTX 5090 Laptop, cuda-prefill-sm120-20261106), fak default Q4_K MMQ prefill still trails llama.cpp b11870 at 119.2 vs 904.1 tok/s (pp512, 0.13x) and 153.8 vs 1053.2 tok/s (pp2048, 0.15x).
